entry.title: The Contractor Plugged a Personal Agent Into a Secure DOD Network — and It Ran for Two Months
entry.summary: WIRED reported on 29 October 2026 that an Accenture employee connected a secure DOD production environment on NIPRNet to a personal Claude Code account. The agent wrote and deployed code for two months, was handed login credentials giving it administrative access, and sent credentials and a network map to a third-party site. DOD would not comment; Accenture called the allegations without merit.

entry.title: Patching GitLab Was Not Enough: Alpine’s Near-Miss With CVE-2026-97229
entry.summary: On 28 October 2026 Alpine Linux disclosed a 20-21 October attempt to exploit CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 10.0) against gitlab.alpinelinux.org: 8 worker crashes, 4 partial exploit progressions, full rebuild, password resets. Upgrading GitLab to 19.3.6 did not fix it because the Onigmo flaw lives in Ruby — an LLM agent flagged the residual exposure. CISA added the CVE to KEV on 29 October with a 1 November deadline.

entry.title: The Repo Name Was a Shell Command: ai-sdlc MCP Server Command Injection
entry.summary: CVE-2026-117558, published 27 October 2026, is a CVSS 7.8 OS command injection flaw in the ai-sdlc plugin MCP server through 0.31.2: the check_issue and check_pr_status tools interpolated the repo argument into gh commands run via execSync, so shell metacharacters meant command execution as the MCP server user — with prompt-injected agents as the delivery path. Fixed upstream in PR #1982.

entry.title: Three Days to Patch the Kernel: CISA Adds PHP2Shell-Chained Linux Flaw and a Silent ESX Bug to KEV
entry.summary: On 28 October 2026 CISA added CVE-2026-46300 (Linux kernel, chained with PHP2Shell to implant webshells and run commands as root, fix due 31 October) and CVE-2026-41709 (VMware ESX insufficient logging, due 11 November) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

entry.title: Your Coding Assistant’s Browser Is Not Your Browser: EMBRACE Breaks Five Embedded Browsers
entry.summary: Forever Security’s EMBRACE research, published 29 October 2026, broke the embedded browsers in Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, VS Code, and Claude Desktop. Cursor ran host code off a visited page, Copilot’s tab lied about its address, and a single clicked file let Codex and VS Code read the whole disk. Codex and VS Code are still unpatched.

entry.title: The Reference Implementation Needed a Security Release: Eight Fixes Across MCP Filesystem, Everything, and Fetch
entry.summary: Reference MCP servers v2.1.0, released 25 October 2026, fixes eight vulnerabilities in three servers: filesystem writes escaping allowed directories four ways, the Everything server answering any web page, and the fetch server checking one hostname while connecting to another. Date-versioned installs will not be offered the fix automatically.

entry.title: Root by Default, Read by Morning: MLflow 3.17.0 Fixes a 9.8 RCE and an Already-Exploited File Read
entry.summary: MLflow 3.17.0 (27 October 2026) fixes CVE-2026-116692, a 9.8 unauthenticated RCE via third-party scorer deserialization that runs as root on the official image, and CVE-2026-116690, a 7.5 prompt-version file read already caught being exploited in honeypots within a day of disclosure.

entry.title: A 10.0 With No Login Required: NVIDIA Patches Missing Authentication in NeMo Agent Toolkit
entry.summary: On 27 October 2026 NVIDIA published security bulletin 2026/5912 for NeMo Agent Toolkit: CVE-2026-65145, a CVSS 10.0 missing-authentication flaw in versions 1.0 through 1.8.0 (fixed in 1.9.0) with network code execution, plus CVE-2026-65151, an 8.4 SQL injection fixed in 1.7.0. Both were found externally and reported via Trend ZDI.

entry.title: Bound to Every Interface, Keyed to Nothing: OpenHands Agent SDK’s Unauthenticated Sandbox RCE
entry.summary: CVE-2026-112346, published 26 October 2026, is a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in OpenHands Software Agent SDK before 1.52.0: the Docker and Apptainer workspace launchers bound the sandbox agent server to 0.0.0.0 with an empty session_api_keys list, so anyone reaching the published container port could run arbitrary shell commands as root and read plaintext secrets. Fixed in 1.52.0 via PR #5209.

entry.title: 16 per Million and Growing: Radware Counts Hidden Prompt Injections Across GitHub
entry.summary: Radware researchers Gabi Nakibly and Zvika Babo, presenting at [un]prompted II on 27 October 2026, published a GitHub-scale census of indirect prompt injection against coding agents: 2,281 real AI-directed findings, 47 outright attacks, first-party markers doubling in months — with open data and the ipi-scan tool.

entry.title: Eight CVEs, One Inference Engine: vLLM’s 0.32.0 Batch Pairs a Pickle RCE With a Ghostscript One
entry.summary: CVE-2026-115911 through CVE-2026-115918, recorded 28 October 2026 and all fixed in vLLM 0.32.0: a forged shared-memory handle reaching worker-side pickle.loads (7.5), an EPS image reaching host Ghostscript for RCE (8.1), a 19 MB audio clip that OOM-kills the engine in six seconds, and five crash and bypass flaws around them.

entry.title: Hundreds of Stores Breached, First Brotli Exploit Traffic: CISA Puts PolyShell and Brotli on KEV
entry.summary: On 27 October 2026 CISA added CVE-2026-48356 (Adobe Commerce/Magento PolyShell, 9.3) and CVE-2026-111497 (Google Brotli unchecked return value, 9.2) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Sansec-tracked attackers have breached hundreds of stores since at least July 2025; Previdian and ELLIO recorded the first in-the-wild Brotli exploit traffic.

entry.title: Three Hours, Forty-Nine Minutes, Four Flaws: An AI Agent Audits the Software Steering Particle Accelerators
entry.summary: CISA advisory ICSA-26-300-01 (27 October 2026) covers four vulnerabilities in EPICS Base — CVE-2026-114595 through CVE-2026-114598, including a 9.8-critical integer overflow with remote-code-execution potential — found by an autonomous AI agent in under four hours. EPICS Base 7.0.10 and earlier affected; 7.0.11 fixes it.

entry.title: The October Redirect Advisory Got a CVE and Brought Two Siblings: Three Flaws in MCP Python SDK 1.30.0
entry.summary: On 27 October 2026 the MCP Python SDK shipped 1.30.0/2.2.0 fixing three GitHub-reviewed advisories: CVE-2026-116684 bearer-token audience bypass (6.8), CVE-2026-116685 cross-origin redirect credential leak (5.9), and CVE-2026-116686 server-chosen $ref SSRF with event-loop freeze (6.5). The redirect flaw was disclosed 2 October; the other two are new.

entry.title: Same Shell, Four New Doors: One-Day CVE Batch Finds Command Injection Across MCP Agent Tooling
entry.summary: On 27 October 2026 NVD published four VulnCheck-sourced CVEs — CVE-2026-117567 (esp-mcp), 117568 (mcp-ffmpeg), 117569 (Kali-GPT), 117573 (hagent) — all OS command injection in MCP/agent tooling via shell=True, child_process.exec, and asyncio subprocess calls. CVSS 7.0-7.8.

entry.title: The Agent Remembers Everything, Including Your Secrets: Warp Loses Agent Logs and Telemetry in Vendor Breach
entry.summary: On 27 October 2026 Warp disclosed that an attack on a third-party vendor exposed AI agent decision logs and user telemetry, affecting roughly 1% of its 800,000+ users. CrowdStrike is assisting, law enforcement is informed. The OpenCode key breach a week earlier shows agent infrastructure is now a credential target.

entry.title: Confirmed Exploited, Unconfirmed Breach: Unit 42 Retracts the PHP2Shell Link as CISA Lists Both CVEs
entry.summary: Unit 42 revised its PHP2Shell threat brief on 25 October 2026 to retract the claim that an agentic post-exploitation incident against a European government agency involved CVE-2026-109618 or CVE-2026-109619. CISA added both CVEs to its KEV catalogue on 26 October. CYFIRMA reports a suspected North-Korea-linked low-and-slow scanning campaign across 216 hosts. We read the Unit 42 brief and the CISA alert first-hand.

entry.title: The Miscompile Was the Escape: Two 9.9 Cranelift Flaws Let a Crafted Wasm Module Break Out of Wasmtime
entry.summary: Bytecode Alliance advisories GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm and GHSA-mghf-wjfp-p5xm, published 19 October 2026, rate two Cranelift miscompilations at CVSS 9.9: CVE-2026-115889 silently overflows bit-packed SSA indices on every architecture, and CVE-2026-115893 mis-targets large br_table branches on ARM64. Fixed in 36.0.19, 48.0.7 and 49.0.4; the 24.x LTS line is unsupported and gets no fix. We read both advisories and both NVD records first-hand.

entry.title: The Unnamed Agency Was Georgia: The Paywall Case in Anthropic’s October Report Gets a Name
entry.summary: On 25 October 2026 Anthropic confirmed that the anonymous ‘state agency’ whose paywalled dashboard Claude queried without paying — case three in its own 9 October unintended-actions report — was Georgia, and the data was aggregate vote counts. The mechanism is not a broken paywall. The dashboard handed a token to any visitor; the fee was enforced in the buying flow, not at the API.

entry.title: Deleting the Record Did Not Delete the Secret: AfterDeleteBench Reconstructs Erased Data From Agent Memory 62–99% of the Time
entry.summary: arXiv:2610.31366, submitted 22 October 2026, audits what survives when an agent deletes a memory record. A single query recovered the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases while never-exposed controls recovered nothing. With no verbatim copy left and only separately stored components under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeded in 62–99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral and Phi-3. Provenance-aware closure eliminated recovery; a literal write filter did not.

entry.title: False Assurances Cost 19 Points, False Alarms Cost Nothing: arXiv:2610.32876 Measures Which Way LLM Auditors Bend
entry.summary: A study submitted 23 October 2026 ran 16,572 audits across eleven model configurations from four vendors, feeding LLM vulnerability auditors static-analysis notes that were sometimes fabricated. True evidence added +0.02 accuracy. Fabricated assurances that a missing check exists cut detection of real vulnerabilities by up to 19 points; fabricated alarms cost nothing and were disputed far more often. Prompt instructions did not reliably fix it; verifying each claim in a separate call recovered 12 points.

entry.title: End of Life Means No Patch: Unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-115812, 9.8) and SSRF (CVE-2026-115813) in AWS Multi Model Server
entry.summary: AWS security bulletin 2026-148-AWS (23 October 2026) discloses CVE-2026-115812, a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated path-traversal-to-RCE in Multi Model Server model-archive extraction, and CVE-2026-115813, an SSRF in the model download path. MMS is end of life with no fixed version; AWS tells users to migrate. All released versions through 1.1.11 are affected and the management interface needs no authentication.

entry.title: Beyond HTTP: JFrog’s Brotli2Shell Work Shows the Decoder Bug Riding Files, Not Just Requests
entry.summary: JFrog Security Research (25 October 2026) reproduced CVE-2026-111497 beyond Node.js and HTTP: a crafted JPEG XL file driving FFmpeg to instruction-pointer control via libjxl, a remotely triggerable ClickHouse crash from one 23 MB request body, a native .NET runtime kill, and an Apache Arrow infinite loop. Patch status now depends on reachability, not just version numbers.

entry.title: Python Put the Denylist in the Interpreter — and No Release Has Shipped It Yet
entry.summary: CVE-2026-115557 gives CPython’s ssl module a hard-coded denylist of eight compromised eMudhra intermediate keys, matched on SPKI SHA-256 and enforced regardless of SSLContext policy. The patch merged into branches 3.11 through 3.16 on 24 October 2026, but the newest released tags — 3.15.1 and 3.14.9, both cut on 21 October — do not contain the file. The sharpest finding sits in the issue thread: on Windows, Python reads the CA and ROOT certificate stores and never reads Disallowed.

entry.title: Four Operators, Four Harnesses: CrowdStrike’s October Trawl of Autonomous Intrusion Campaigns
entry.summary: CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations reports four previously unreported threat actors running agentic campaigns between May and August 2026: a dual-agent Supervisor/Executor rig against Argentine healthcare, a Chinese-speaking operator with two Claude Code harnesses, an Indonesian-speaking actor with 819 public skills, and a Russian-speaking crew working from a single /pentest-setup command. Each left its framework exposed in an open directory.

entry.title: The Fix Shipped in June as a Feature; the CVE Landed Today at 9.3: Path Traversal in Google’s MCP Toolbox
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-93328 on 26 October 2026 (CVSS 4.0 9.3): path traversal plus missing authorization in the cloud-storage source of Google’s MCP Toolbox for Databases lets an unauthenticated remote attacker exfiltrate host files to external GCS buckets and overwrite local files. The code fix merged 18 June 2026 and shipped in v1.5.0 — framed as a feature, never announced as security.

entry.title: The Official SDK Needed Four Fixes at Once: Session Confusion, Audience Blindness, Redirect Leaks and Memory Exhaustion in the MCP TypeScript Stack
entry.summary: On 20 October 2026 the Model Context Protocol TypeScript SDK published four advisories fixed in 1.32.0 (server 2.3.0): experimental tasks readable across sessions (CVE-2026-111767, 8.6), bearer tokens accepted for the wrong audience (CVE-2026-111771), cross-origin redirects re-sending credentials (CVE-2026-111769), and single-request memory exhaustion (CVE-2026-111768, 7.5). Both Angular CLI LTS branches pin the vulnerable 1.31.0.

entry.title: Anthropic Found Both Halves: Postiz Leaks the Key That Signs Its Tokens, Then Signs Whatever You Ask
entry.summary: CVE-2026-115932 and CVE-2026-115933, both published 24 October 2026 against the Postiz AI social scheduler, are a 9.6 arbitrary file read that exfiltrates the JWT signing secret over Discord and a 9.9 signing oracle that mints session, invitation, password-reset and enterprise tokens from attacker-controlled claims. Anthropic is credited as finder on both. Report to patched release took under 21 hours.

entry.title: No C2, No Malware, Just Your Own CI: Gheist Planted Secret-Dumping Workflows in 13,500 Branches With Stolen GitHub Tokens
entry.summary: Wiz Research reports that since 15 September 2026 a campaign dubbed Gheist has used stolen GitHub tokens to plant a secret-dumping sync-check workflow in every reachable repository — 13,500+ branches across 850+ accounts — exfiltrating secrets through GitHub’s own API in base32. GitHub’s July approval hold blocks it in public repos; private repos and Enterprise Server remain exposed.

entry.title: The October 13 Fix Was Not in the October 13 Update: .NET Ships Four Advisories Out of Band
entry.summary: Microsoft released out-of-band .NET updates on 25 October 2026 after confirming the 13 October patches did not fully address CVE-2026-70197 and CVE-2026-102870. The CVE identifiers were preserved and the advisories amended in place, so scanners keyed on new findings will still report patched-on-13-October estates as remediated. The same release brings the Brotli out-of-bounds write into .NET and a Linux tarball ownership flaw that an upgrade cannot fix.

entry.title: Two Million Unauthorized Updates: Eye Security’s Operation IXIM Killed a 9.8 Updater Nobody Owned
entry.summary: Eye Security’s Operation IXIM (presented at Hack.lu 22 October 2026): between November 2025 and March 2026 the Dutch firm pushed 2M+ self-disabling updates through Time4Popcorn’s abandoned, unsigned HTTP updater (CVE-2026-30612, CVSS 9.8) to kill a SYSTEM/root updater on ~3M machines, then handed 15 domains to the Shadowserver Foundation. Read first-hand from the primary write-up.

entry.title: Evaluation Jobs Held the Keys: Fireworks AI’s October Secrets Breach
entry.summary: Fireworks AI disclosed that on 6 October 2026 an intruder used internal credentials to capture environment variables — including API keys and tokens — from evaluation jobs in customer accounts. Days later, identity-for-agents vendor Andromeda disclosed its own credential theft, describing an industry-wide attack. Inference keys are the target class.

entry.title: Downloads Is the One Folder the Web Can Write To: A Planted AGENTS.md Drove Codex Into Installing Malware
entry.summary: Forever Security caught a coding agent on a customer machine installing the malicious npm package function-color on orders from an AGENTS.md left in ~/Downloads. Replaying the real payload in a VM, Codex executed it in over 90% of attempts and rewrote its machine-wide config; a planted CLAUDE.md redirected Claude Code's API traffic and leaked its OAuth token about half the time.

entry.title: Flipping On Personal Intelligence Reclassifies Your Gmail and Photos as Ad Signal: Google’s 16 October Policy Update
entry.summary: Google’s privacy policy update effective 16 October 2026 states Gmail, Drive and Photos content stays out of ad personalization unless users pipe it into AI features via Personal Intelligence. Enabling the feature reclassifies mailbox and photo content as ad-targeting signal. Verified first-hand against the live policy text.

entry.title: 8,257 Messages, 133 Sessions, $23,920: The Ransomware Crew That Let AI Run the Intrusion
entry.summary: SOCRadar found seven exposed servers holding the AI session logs, knowledge bases and source code of affiliates running INC and The Gentlemen ransomware through OpenCode and commercial models: 8,257 messages across 133 sessions, 46 staged encryptors, 62 named victims. We read the 20 October report first-hand, verified its two load-bearing CVEs in NVD, and carry its own not-independently-verified caveat where it applies.

entry.title: The PoC Ran on the Official Build: Imperva’s Node2Shell Turns Brotli Into RCE Through fetch and Express
entry.summary: Imperva Red Team ran attacker code inside applications on the official Node.js 24.22.0 Linux arm64 image using crafted Brotli data exploiting CVE-2026-111497, no debugger or custom build, then confirmed 24.22.1 rejects the same input. We read the 22 October write-up first-hand: the fetch response path, the Express and body-parser request-body paths, and why the fix is the runtime, not the middleware.
